q: Complete the analogy: Bird is to nest as bee is to ___.
e: A bird lives in a nest; a bee lives in a hive.

q: Complete the analogy: Lion is to den as rabbit is to ___.
e: A lion uses a den; a rabbit uses a burrow.

q: Complete the analogy: Horse is to stable as dog is to ___.
e: A horse is kept in a stable; a dog is kept in a kennel.

q: Complete the analogy: Sheep is to flock as fish is to ___.
e: A group of sheep is a flock; a group of fish is a school.

q: Complete the analogy: Wolf is to pack as bee is to ___.
e: A group of wolves is a pack; a group of bees is a swarm.

q: Complete the analogy: Author is to book as composer is to ___.
e: An author creates a book; a composer creates music.

q: Complete the analogy: Painter is to canvas as writer is to ___.
e: A painter works on canvas; a writer works on a page.

q: Complete the analogy: Doctor is to hospital as teacher is to ___.
e: A doctor commonly works in a hospital; a teacher works in a school.

q: Complete the analogy: Judge is to court as pilot is to ___.
e: A judge works in a court; a pilot operates from a cockpit.

q: Complete the analogy: Chef is to kitchen as mechanic is to ___.
e: A chef works in a kitchen; a mechanic works in a garage.

q: Complete the analogy: Knife is to cut as pen is to ___.
e: A knife is used to cut; a pen is used to write.

q: Complete the analogy: Needle is to sew as brush is to ___.
e: A needle is used to sew; a brush is used to paint.

q: Complete the analogy: Thermometer is to temperature as clock is to ___.
e: A thermometer measures temperature; a clock measures time.

q: Complete the analogy: Scale is to weight as ruler is to ___.
e: A scale measures weight; a ruler measures length.

q: Complete the analogy: Compass is to direction as calendar is to ___.
e: A compass indicates direction; a calendar indicates date.

q: Complete the analogy: Sapling is to tree as calf is to ___.
e: A sapling grows into a tree; a calf grows into a cow.

q: Complete the analogy: Caterpillar is to butterfly as tadpole is to ___.
e: A caterpillar develops into a butterfly; a tadpole develops into a frog.

q: Complete the analogy: Bud is to flower as egg is to ___.
e: A bud develops into a flower; an egg can develop into a bird.

q: Complete the analogy: Puppy is to dog as kitten is to ___.
e: A puppy is a young dog; a kitten is a young cat.

q: Complete the analogy: Foal is to horse as lamb is to ___.
e: A foal is a young horse; a lamb is a young sheep.

q: Complete the analogy: Hot is to cold as early is to ___.
e: Hot and cold are opposites; early and late are opposites.

q: Complete the analogy: Expand is to contract as accept is to ___.
e: Expand and contract are opposites; accept and reject are opposites.

q: Complete the analogy: Victory is to defeat as arrival is to ___.
e: Victory and defeat are opposites; arrival and departure are opposites.

q: Complete the analogy: Generous is to stingy as brave is to ___.
e: Generous and stingy are opposites; brave and cowardly are opposites.

q: Complete the analogy: Ancient is to modern as scarce is to ___.
e: Ancient and modern are opposites; scarce and abundant are opposites.

q: Complete the analogy: Glove is to hand as shoe is to ___.
e: A glove is worn on a hand; a shoe is worn on a foot.

q: Complete the analogy: Helmet is to head as ring is to ___.
e: A helmet is worn on the head; a ring is worn on a finger.

q: Complete the analogy: Roof is to house as lid is to ___.
e: A roof covers a house; a lid covers a box.

q: Complete the analogy: Bark is to tree as skin is to ___.
e: Bark covers a tree; skin covers a body.

q: Complete the analogy: Key is to lock as password is to ___.
e: A key gives access through a lock; a password gives access to an account.

q: Complete the analogy: Chapter is to book as scene is to ___.
e: A chapter is a part of a book; a scene is a part of a play.

q: Complete the analogy: Minute is to hour as day is to ___.
e: A minute is a unit within an hour; a day is a unit within a week.

q: Complete the analogy: Petal is to flower as page is to ___.
e: A petal is part of a flower; a page is part of a book.

q: Complete the analogy: Finger is to hand as toe is to ___.
e: A finger is part of a hand; a toe is part of a foot.

q: Complete the analogy: Branch is to tree as tributary is to ___.
e: A branch extends from a tree; a tributary joins and forms part of a river system.

q: Complete the analogy: Oxygen is to breathe as water is to ___.
e: Oxygen is taken in for breathing; water is taken in for drinking.

q: Complete the analogy: Fuel is to engine as food is to ___.
e: Fuel supplies energy to an engine; food supplies energy to the body.

q: Complete the analogy: Eyes is to see as ears is to ___.
e: Eyes are used to see; ears are used to hear.

q: Complete the analogy: Tongue is to taste as nose is to ___.
e: The tongue senses taste; the nose senses smell.

q: Complete the analogy: Library is to books as museum is to ___.
e: A library houses books; a museum houses artifacts.

q: Which item is the odd one out among Oak, Rose, Tulip and Lily?
e: Rose, tulip and lily are flowers; oak is a tree.

q: Which item is the odd one out among Copper, Plastic, Iron and Gold?
e: Copper, iron and gold are metals; plastic is not.

q: Which item is the odd one out among Eagle, Sparrow, Bat and Pigeon?
e: Eagle, Sparrow and Pigeon are birds; a bat is a mammal.

q: Which item is the odd one out among Carrot, Potato, Radish and Apple?
e: Carrot, Potato and Radish are root vegetables; apple is a fruit.

q: Which item is the odd one out among Monday, January, March and July?
e: January, March and July are months; Monday is a day of the week.

q: Which item is the odd one out among Circle, Cylinder, Triangle and Square?
e: Circle, Triangle and Square are plane figures; cylinder is a solid.

q: Which item is the odd one out among Piano, Violin, Hammer and Flute?
e: Piano, Violin and Flute are musical instruments; a hammer is a tool.

q: Which item is the odd one out among Mercury, Venus, Mars and Moon?
e: Mercury, Venus and Mars are planets; the Moon is a natural satellite.

q: Which item is the odd one out among Dolphin, Shark, Salmon and Trout?
e: Shark, Salmon and Trout are fish; a dolphin is a mammal.

q: Which item is the odd one out among Cotton, Glass, Wool and Silk?
e: Cotton, Wool and Silk are textile fibres; glass is not.
